subject: Short pilot runway — billing structure options and next steps
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ramos <sofia@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Short pilot runway — billing structure options and next steps

Hi Sofia —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Acme's usage patterns look encouraging — your team is running a concentrated set of workflows over short bursts which is a good fit for a time-boxed pilot, but I hear you on predictability for billing while product validation is ongoing. To unblock the evaluation quickly, we can do one of the two pragmatic options below. Please tell me which you'd prefer and whether procurement prefers an invoice/PO or a DocuSign amendment.

Option A — 2-week extension (timebox)
- Add 14 calendar days to the existing pilot window.
- Fixed fee: $6,400 (covers up to the burst profile we saw; overages billed at standard PAYG).
- No credits; clean short amendment.

Option B — Top-up credits (flex bucket)
- Add a 10k-token credit bucket for $4,800 usable over 30 days.
- Credits are consumed first; any overage billed monthly.
- Better if you want to smooth consumption across teams.

Sizing note: either path keeps the current SLA and access to our dedicated pilot capacity for the duration. I've attached the pricing_breakdown.xlsx and pilot-usage-metrics.csv so you can see the expected burn estimates.

Quick ask: can you let me know by EOD Friday which option procurement prefers, and whether they need an invoice/PO or DocuSign for approval? If useful, we can also do a hybrid (short extension + small credit) — Ben and Marissa on CC can confirm internal approvals.

Thanks,
Logan Wright

Logan —

Thanks for laying out the choices. A few quick questions to make sure procurement can approve:
1) For Option A, does the fixed fee invoice immediately on amendment signature or at the end of the 14 days?
2) For Option B, do credits expire at day 30 exactly or at the end of the calendar month?
3) If we choose the hybrid, will invoices split into two line items (extension + credits)?

Also: we need confirmation that the pilot's dedicated capacity and performance targets stay unchanged during the extension. We can't risk throttling mid-eval.

Procurement prefers an invoice + PO flow, but if Redwood can send a short amendment via DocuSign that generates an invoice, that works too.

Looping in our pricing/finance POV. Given Acme's usage profile and the ask that capacity not be impacted, my suggestion is a compromise that reduces friction for procurement while keeping the pilot economics reasonable for Redwood:

Counter (recommended)
- 10 calendar day extension (shorter than option A) + $3,000 credit applied at sign.
- Invoice structure: single invoice covering the extension fee ($3,400) and credit allocation ($3,000) split into two line items so Acme can PO each line.
- Credits expire 30 days from activation (keeps bookkeeping simple).

Rationale: shorter extension reduces our reserved window risk; the credit gives them cushion for bursts and makes procurement happy with a PO. We can honor the current performance profile and guarantee the pilot priority throughout the extension (ops will reserve capacity).

I'm attaching a short counter_offer_summary.pdf you can forward instead of the full XLSX if procurement requests less detail.

- Ben
